answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to post a refundable bond that grows with influence: to vote, trade, or grade, an agent locks stake, and proven fraud slashes it. An honest agent pays once, like mooring a single boat at a jetty. A sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every fake, each tinted with its own pigment of fabricated history, so multiplying identities multiplies capital at risk rather than power — and exposure slashes the whole fleet at once, with no sonnet of excuses earning a refund.
